modelResponse.episodeSummary: James P. Whitfield, 61M, Ventricular Tachycardia, critical, hemodynamically unstable
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Wide monomorphic QRS, AV dissociation, occasional capture/fusion beats
contributingFactors: Underlying structural heart disease (Ischemic cardiomyopathy, LVEF 25%)
Possible electrolyte imbalance (though K 4.3 is normal)

rejectedAlternatives.why: QTc is null, but baseline QTc was normal (460 ms) and morphology is monomorphic, not polymorphic.
AV dissociation and fusion beats are present, strongly suggesting VT. QRS duration is wide (168 ms).
Rate is too fast (182 bpm) and rhythm is regular, whereas AIVR is typically slower and irregular.

recommendedActions: Assess for reversible causes (e.g., ischemia, electrolyte abnormalities, hypoxia)
Consider Lidocaine 1-1.5 mg/kg IV push if Amiodarone is ineffective or contraindicated
Withhold digoxin if patient was on it (not listed, but check)
uncertainty: Exact cause of VT (ischemia vs. structural) cannot be definitively determined without further workup.
QTc interval is missing, limiting assessment for Torsades.
